findings.Fix: Cut the aside: "If the hunter was running the same trail backward, he'd arrive here."

findings.Quote: Fast and unhurried at once, the economy of someone who'd done this when it was legal and hadn't forgotten how.
findings.Note: Paradox-phrasing ('fast and unhurried at once') is a stock construction that asserts skill rather than demonstrating it.
findings.Fix: Show a specific gesture — e.g. how she ties off, how her hands move — instead of naming the contradiction.

findings.Quote: His eyes were cleaner than they'd been all night — the last dose had worn through and he hadn't reached for the vial.
findings.Note: Sits awkwardly against the following sentence's claim the dark 'had nothing to do with the drug,' undercutting the causal link just established.
findings.Fix: Pick one causal thread — either the drug clarity or the room's weight — and don't assert both then deny the connection.

findings.Quote: that was the whole point of his hands
findings.Fix: cut or replace with something concrete about his training/reputation

findings.Quote: the tray was a thing he could survive looking at
findings.Fix: consider tightening; borderline aphoristic phrasing

findings.Quote: his stomach did a slow turn he hadn't ordered
findings.Fix: replace with a more specific, less stock bodily reaction

findings.Quote: the only thing in the room that asked nothing of him but skill
findings.Fix: trim the aphoristic close; let the action stand alone

findings.Quote: None of them ever made me want to wash my hands.
findings.Note: Vague gesture-at-meaning line; tells us she feels dirty without grounding the image in anything specific about this man.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete detail about what he did that unsettled her.

findings.Quote: the sky over the lower Ward had gone the color it went before dawn — not light yet, just less dark
findings.Note: Familiar pre-dawn sky description dressed up but still a stock beat/transition device.
findings.Fix: Anchor it to something specific to this setting (smog color, neon dying, etc.) rather than generic dawn language.

findings.Quote: a city that woke and started counting its sons
findings.Note: Slightly overreaching personification/aphorism-adjacent phrasing that leans poetic without earning it.
findings.Fix: Simplify to a more concrete stake: 'before someone noticed the heir was missing.'

findings.Quote: three Lotus men in a parked car across the street who weren't pretending to be anything else
findings.Note: Tells us their obviousness rather than showing a concrete detail that makes them legible as watchers.
findings.Fix: Give one specific visual (engine running, matching jackets, one man not looking at his phone) instead of asserting the conclusion.

findings.Quote: so ordinary it was furniture
findings.Note: the simile is doing a job the following sentence already does more concretely; it reads as a placeholder abstraction rather than an image that holds up to scrutiny
findings.Fix: cut the furniture comparison and let 'decent people looked away' carry the ordinariness

findings.Quote: the way, Tomas would understand later, he laid it when he wanted you to know he wasn't, yet, reaching for it
findings.Note: the flash-forward qualifier is clunky mechanically (double comma-break, 'wasn't, yet, reaching') and tells us the meaning of the gesture rather than trusting the image
findings.Fix: tighten to something like 'the way he laid it when he wanted you to know he wasn't reaching for it yet' and cut the 'Tomas would understand later' frame

findings.Quote: a man reciting the terms of his own life like a weather report
findings.Note: Simile is serviceable but leans toward stock 'flat affect' imagery and slightly overexplains the tone already conveyed by 'flat, tired.'
findings.Fix: Trim to 'flat, tired, like he'd said it before' or cut the simile entirely.

findings.Quote: letting him make the last move himself
findings.Note: slightly redundant filler explaining the manipulation tactic already shown by the dialogue itself
findings.Fix: cut the clause or fold it into fewer words, e.g. 'not selling, just laying the pieces where the man could see them.'

findings.Quote: The room was very quiet.
findings.Note: generic tension-beat filler phrase, stock silence marker
findings.Fix: specify a concrete sensory detail unique to the room instead of the generic 'very quiet.'

findings.Quote: They don't seat you at the table. They feed you under it.
findings.Note: Aphoristic parallelism that reads as a crafted maxim rather than something a man would say mid-threat; slightly too polished for the register.
findings.Fix: Cut the second sentence, let the first stand alone: "They don't seat you at the table."

findings.Quote: the soft son, the bloodline made flesh, the thing the whole machine existed to protect
findings.Note: Triple restatement of the same idea in escalating abstraction is padding, not escalation.
findings.Fix: Cut to one phrase: "the soft son the whole machine existed to protect."

findings.Quote: a man about to kill you doesn't let his hands go easy
findings.Note: Reads as an inserted rule/aphorism about violence rather than Tomas's perception in the moment; slightly too neat and generalized.
findings.Fix: Ground it in Tomas's specific read: "but Ekow's hands had already gone loose at his sides."

findings.Quote: something almost like the nod one disposable man gives another over a body
findings.Note: Abstract, overwrought construction ('one disposable man gives another') states the thematic point rather than showing a concrete gesture.
findings.Fix: Simplify to the physical action: "something almost like a nod passed between them."

findings.Quote: the dog the Lotus kept for finding things showed them where the seams went
findings.Note: Metaphor collapses under literal scrutiny — a dog trained for finding things doesn't logically show people narrative 'seams'; the image is decorative rather than functional and obscures what's actually happening in the scene.
findings.Fix: Either show the dog performing a concrete action (sniffing out a flaw in the staged scene) or cut the clause.

findings.Quote: the grammar of a bender gone over a cliff
findings.Note: 'Grammar of' is a worn intellectualizing metaphor for staged evidence, and 'gone over a cliff' is a stock idiom for excess/disaster.
findings.Fix: Cut to plain description: 'they laid out the evidence of a bender gone too far.'

findings.Quote: The wreck of a last free night thrown away by a soft rich boy with one day left before the rest of his life.
findings.Note: This reads as authorial summary/telling rather than an observed detail of the scene — it editorializes the boy's character ('soft rich boy') rather than showing it through the staged objects.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence or ground it in a physical detail that implies the same judgment.

findings.Quote: This is the same work with the arrows turned around.
findings.Note: A tidy aphoristic summation of Ekow's moral position — reads as a crafted line of wisdom rather than something a man would say mid-task, veering toward pseudo-profound.
findings.Fix: Trim to something more clipped and functional: 'Same work. Arrows just point the other way.'

findings.Quote: That was the thing he held onto. The only thing.
findings.Note: Telling-not-showing the emotional stakes; the fragment reads as an imposed emphasis rather than earned weight.
findings.Fix: Cut the second sentence, or replace with a concrete action showing him holding onto that thought.

findings.Quote: He understood, without being told, that this wasn't a body the two of them would let a stranger's hands move.
findings.Note: Explains the preceding scene's meaning rather than trusting the dialogue and action already shown; slightly redundant summary.
findings.Fix: Cut or fold into action, e.g., show him stepping back rather than stating his understanding.

findings.Quote: which was its own kind of saying
findings.Note: Aphoristic tag that explains the silence rather than letting it stand; slightly pat phrasing.
findings.Fix: End the beat on the silence itself without the summarizing clause.

findings.Quote: not one true thing in the whole tableau except that both people in that bed had been failed by everyone who was supposed to keep them
findings.Note: tips into aphoristic summary that tells us the moral of the scene instead of trusting the image
findings.Fix: cut the 'except' clause or make it more specific to these two people

findings.Quote: the closest he came all night to something with an edge of pleasure on it
findings.Note: vague hedge-phrase describing an emotion instead of showing it in action or dialogue
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete physical tell (a flicker of a smile, a slower exhale)

findings.Quote: because no one will think to look, and neither will they
findings.Note: redundant repetition of 'think to look' from two sentences earlier weakens the line's punch
findings.Fix: vary the phrasing so the repetition reads as intentional rhetoric, not a slip

findings.Quote: no completion to log, no account to flip, no number going to zero
findings.Note: triplet list leans on parallel-structure rhythm as a substitute for a sharper single image, feels like padding toward a thesis statement
findings.Fix: cut to one or two items instead of three

findings.Quote: were furniture, were garbagemen, were invisible
findings.Note: triplet is doing overwrought poetic labor for what's essentially 'they held still and looked ordinary'; the abstraction (furniture, invisible) undercuts the concrete tension of the moment
findings.Fix: cut to two: 'were garbagemen, were nobody'

findings.Quote: Breathing started again somewhere around the time its taillights turned the corner
findings.Note: held-breath-release is a stock tension beat
findings.Fix: anchor it to a physical, specific detail instead of the generic breath resume

findings.Quote: it sat on him lightly now, lighter than it had any right to
findings.Note: vague interiority stating the exhaustion's effect without grounding it in sensation
findings.Fix: replace with one concrete physical marker of the false lightness

findings.Quote: a thing was already true that none of them had read yet
findings.Note: Vague abstraction standing in for concrete stakes; tells rather than shows what the 'thing' is.
findings.Fix: Name the fact obliquely but concretely, e.g. 'behind which the heir was already dead, though none of them had read it yet.'

findings.Quote: He watched the car become four cars.
findings.Note: Cute construction that slightly undercuts the tension with cleverness rather than dread.
findings.Fix: Consider flattening: 'Three more cars arrived within minutes.'

findings.Quote: He turned the word over and found it good.
findings.Note: Slightly precious phrasing ('found it good') edges toward aphoristic self-congratulation rather than character interiority.
findings.Fix: 'He turned the word over. It suited him.'

findings.Quote: a sentence with his name in it
findings.Note: vague metaphor standing in for concrete stakes; doesn't specify what the sentence is
findings.Fix: name the actual consequence (loss of license, debt, exile) instead of the abstract phrase

findings.Quote: beginning — quietly, two floors up — to eat itself
findings.Note: mixed literal/figurative image; a house eating itself two floors up strains visualization
findings.Fix: anchor to a concrete sound or action happening two floors up rather than the abstract 'eat itself'

findings.Quote: dark and patient
findings.Note: stock personification pairing for ominous vehicles
findings.Fix: specify a sensory detail unique to this wagon instead of the generic dark/patient pairing

findings.Quote: a city that was about to get very loud behind him
findings.Note: vague foreshadowing filler that tells rather than shows the coming conflict
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete sensory cue of the coming unrest

findings.Quote: The wind came off the water flat and cold and asked him for nothing.
findings.Note: Personification of wind as asking is a slightly strained anthropomorphic conceit, though the follow-up sentence justifies it somewhat.
findings.Fix: Consider grounding the metaphor more concretely, e.g. tying it directly to a specific demand he's used to hearing.

findings.Quote: he felt it the way you feel a fire once you're far enough away that it's only warmth on your back
findings.Note: Second-person address ('you feel') breaks close third POV voice and reads as a generalized aphorism rather than his specific sensation.
findings.Fix: Rephrase in his own perspective: 'the way heat reaches you long after you've stopped watching the flame' or similar, keeping it in third person.

findings.Quote: Ten years of arriving after the ending. This time he'd been early.
findings.Note: Reads as a neat, quotable summary line that tells us the thematic point rather than letting the preceding image carry it — verges on pseudo-profound capstone.
findings.Fix: Cut or fold the realization into action/interiority tied to a concrete detail from this scene.

findings.Quote: marking things was the last of what the work had left in him
findings.Note: Slightly abstract self-diagnosis stated rather than demonstrated; borders on telling not showing his depletion.
findings.Fix: Show the marking itself with more physical specificity and let the depletion be implied.

findings.Quote: He looked like a man waiting for a knock he wasn't sure was coming.
findings.Note: Slightly redundant with the preceding image (already sitting, coat on, reconsidered) — restates the same uncertainty in a vaguer, more abstract way, weakening the concrete visual just established.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence or replace with a concrete physical detail (e.g. a specific gesture).

findings.Quote: the way a man speaks when he's holding something he isn't sure won't break
findings.Note: Generic simile for careful speech; doesn't add specific sensory or character information beyond 'careful.'
findings.Fix: Cut the simile and let 'careful' stand alone, or ground it in a physical action Levin actually does.

findings.Quote: holding everything on the company's books that wasn't attached to a person yet
findings.Note: vague euphemistic phrasing that tells rather than shows what the lockers actually contain
findings.Fix: specify concretely what the inventory is, or cut the qualifier

findings.Quote: the cursor blinking on a decision he wasn't ready to make
findings.Note: stock image of hesitation-via-cursor reads as filler rather than earned interiority
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a more specific physical detail of his stalling

findings.Quote: they had to be, given the inventory
findings.Note: glib aside undercuts the horror of the moment with a quippy justification
findings.Fix: cut the clause or replace with a flatter, harder statement of fact

findings.Quote: The elevator took forty-five seconds, same as before.
findings.Note: Oddly precise timing stated flatly reads as filler specificity rather than meaningful detail.
findings.Fix: Cut the number or tie it to a character's impatience/awareness.

findings.Quote: the careful attention of someone who'd signed her name before on things she didn't fully understand
findings.Note: Tells the reader about her backstory/character rather than showing it through concrete detail; feels like a generalized character summary dropped in.
findings.Fix: Show a concrete detail instead, e.g. her finger tracing each line, lips moving over unfamiliar words.

findings.Quote: "What kind of discrepancy?" she asks.
findings.Note: Tense shifts from past ("said," "looked") to present ("asks") mid-scene, an inconsistency in narration.
findings.Fix: Change to "she asked."

findings.Quote: because there wasn't anything useful to say, and because *change of heart* had covered it about as well as anything was going to
findings.Note: Hedging, vague telling-not-showing of an internal state; leans on abstraction instead of a concrete beat.
findings.Fix: Cut the second clause or replace with a specific concrete detail of what he almost said.

findings.Quote: tall and grey and indifferent
findings.Note: Stock city-personification triplet, generic and unearned emotional coloring.
findings.Fix: Cut the adjective string or replace with one concrete visual detail specific to this city.

findings.Quote: He'd learned not to describe it.
findings.Note: Tells us he avoids description while the narration just described it, undercutting itself without irony intended.
findings.Fix: Cut the line or make the contradiction pointed/intentional.

findings.Quote: it cost him something, the way everything did now
findings.Note: Vague abstraction stating emotional cost without specifying it, echoing the chapter title too neatly as a thesis-statement line.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete physical tell of the cost (a held breath, a flinch) instead of naming the abstraction.

findings.Quote: kept it the way you keep a thing you can't bear to look at
findings.Note: Generic aphoristic phrasing that tells the emotion rather than showing it, slightly deflating the specificity of the image before it.
findings.Fix: Cut the generalization; let the action (not looking) carry the meaning.

findings.Quote: his sick clean shaking hands
findings.Note: Stacked adjectives read as a list rather than an image; unclear what 'clean' is doing next to 'sick' and 'shaking' without more context.
findings.Fix: Pick one or two precise details, e.g. 'his shaking, too-clean hands.'

findings.Quote: the account he'd have to fill again one body at a time
findings.Note: Slightly abstract phrasing for what should be a concrete transactional image given the novel's economy of debt/bodies; reads as a placeholder metaphor.
findings.Fix: Specify what filling the account means in body/debt terms already established.

findings.Quote: a photograph of a man who used to squint into a better sun
findings.Note: 'a better sun' is a soft poetic abstraction bordering on cliché nostalgia-shorthand, undercutting the harder, specific imagery established in ref 0.
findings.Fix: Tie the image back to the concrete detail already given, e.g. 'a photograph of a man who used to squint into sun that wasn't the GLMZ.'
